seo.title: Greedy Algorithms: The Sort Key Is The Whole Puzzle
seo.hook: Four meetings, three blocks of time. The sort does most of the work. But which sort?
seo.description: You can merge or schedule intervals in one pass, once you know what to sort by.

scenes.narration: Four meetings, three blocks of time. The sort does most of the work. But which sort?

scenes.headline: Overlap, so [merge]
scenes.caption: two into one
scenes.narration: |The diary is sorted by start time, and the next booking is ^two to six. |Does its start come before the current block ends? Two is less than or equal to three, so yes, they overlap. |So we stretch the block's end to whichever end is later, which is six. ^One to three and two to six have become ^one to six. %One block now covers both meetings, and notice we never created anything new, we only widened what was already there.

lines.detail: Walk the rest, in sorted order.
Does this one start before the block ends?
Then stretch the block to the later end.

scenes.premise: A meeting-room diary. Each bar is one booking drawn on a shared timeline, so two bars that overlap are two meetings that clash.

scenes.headline: A gap, so [start again]
scenes.caption: a second block
scenes.narration: |Next is ^eight to ten. Does eight come before six? It doesn't, so there's a gap. |The else branch runs and we append it as ^a separate block. %Two blocks now. That's the entire decision the algorithm ever makes: overlap means widen, gap means append. One comparison per booking, and it never revisits a decision it has already taken. That refusal to look back is exactly what the word greedy means.

lines.detail: Eight does not start before six. No overlap.
So this becomes a block of its own.

scenes.premise: A meeting-room diary. Each bar is one booking drawn on a shared timeline, so two bars that overlap are two meetings that clash.

scenes.headline: And the [last one]
scenes.caption: three blocks, done
scenes.narration: |Last booking, ^fifteen to eighteen. Fifteen is well past ten, so another gap, and it becomes ^a third block. |Return merged, and %the diary is three blocks instead of four bookings. The whole thing cost one sort plus one walk, which is n log n for the sort and n for the walk. The sort dominates, so the honest complexity to quote is n log n.
